Why Georgia Tech's Paul Johnson still runs option offense, and why it still works

It's definitely fun to watch and he makes a good point about signing-in plays: If you can decipher the signs to it and have any kind of decent defense, you can put a strain on an opposing hurry-up offense. And the option, as run by Johnson, is the anti-air-raid. When you're punishing defenses for hanging back and waiting on the run, you can start pulling them in tighter and tighter until you can throw over their heads and tear off a huge pass (think Saban's National Championship teams: Pound it in with a lot of runs, force the defense to move in, and spring a long pass when they can't defend it). The only big problem with skewing the run/pass numbers so far to one side is that you risk having to rely on something you don't do often (possibly not that well, depending on circumstances) and getting pushed into playing the opposing defense's game.
